content:
One chapter in Class 8 pays for itself in every later class: solving equations with x on both sides. The method never changes. The IMO simply keeps raising the disguise — fractions, brackets, then a boat moving upstream. Start by testing the ground. The free IMO Class 8 Linear Equations online test below asks 10 exam-pattern MCQs and scores them on the spot. Each explanation shows the intended one-minute route.

What the IMO asks from Linear Equations in Class 8

  • Equations with the variable on both sides.
  • Fraction coefficients — clear them with the LCM in one move.
  • Equations reducible to linear form by cross-multiplication.
  • Number, digit and age problems.
  • Perimeter, money and speed set-ups that produce equations.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • For x/2 − x/5 = 6, multiply through by 10 and the fractions vanish: 5x − 2x = 60.
  • Cross-multiplication: (x + 1)/(2x + 3) = 3/8 means 8(x + 1) = 3(2x + 3).
  • A two-digit number is 10t + u — writing this line first unlocks every digit puzzle.
  • Always substitute the answer back; ten seconds buys a guaranteed mark.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Transposing a term without flipping its sign.
  • Distributing 3(2x − 1) as 6x − 1.
  • Solving for x correctly, then forgetting the question asked for the NUMBER, not x.

questions.explanation: Transpose variable terms: 5x - 3x = 9 + 7. Simplify: 2x = 16. Divide both sides by 2: x = 8.
Expand left: 12x - 3 - 6x - 10 = 6x - 13. Expand right: 4x - 8. Equation: 6x - 13 = 4x - 8. Transpose: 2x = 5, so x = 5/2.

Using the identity a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b) with a = 3x + 2 and b = 3x - 2: (6x)(4) = 60. So 24x = 60, giving x = 60/24 = 5/2.
LCD is 15. Multiply through: 3(3x + 4) - 5(x - 2) = 30. Expand: 9x + 12 - 5x + 10 = 30. Simplify: 4x + 22 = 30, so 4x = 8, giving x = 2.
LCD is 15. Multiply through: 3(3x + 2) - 5(2x - 1) = (x + 4) + 15. Expand: 9x + 6 - 10x + 5 = x + 19. Simplify: -x + 11 = x + 19. Transpose: -8 = 2x, so x = -4.

questions.q: A number is 12 more than twice another number. If their sum is 78, find the larger number.
questions.explanation: Let the smaller number be x. The larger is 2x + 12. Sum: x + (2x + 12) = 78, so 3x + 12 = 78. Solving: 3x = 66, x = 22. The larger number is 2(22) + 12 = 56.

questions.q: Ravi is 4 years older than twice Sita's age. If the sum of their ages is 37 years, how old is Ravi?
questions.explanation: Let Sita's age be x. Ravi's age = 2x + 4. Sum: x + (2x + 4) = 37, so 3x + 4 = 37. Solving: 3x = 33, x = 11. Ravi's age = 2(11) + 4 = 26.

questions.q: A train covers a certain distance at 60 km/h. If it had travelled 10 km/h faster, it would have taken 1 hour less. Find the distance.
